chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) sent for me and Muhammad ibn Hamza during his illness. So Muhammad ibn Hamza preceded me to go to him, and Muhammad informed me, 'He did not cease saying, 'Go to al-Hayr, go to al-Hayr!' So I said to Muhammad, 'Did you not say to him that I am going to al-Hayr?' Then I went over to him and said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I am going to al-Hayr'. So he said: 'Look into that'.

Then he said to me: 'Muhammad, there is a secret for him from Zayd ibn Ali, and I dislike it that he should hear that'. So I mentioned that to Ali ibn Bilal, and he said, 'What does he have to do with al-Hayr and he (himself) is (from) al-Hayr?' So I proceeded to al-Askar and I went over to him. So he said to me: 'Be seated!', when I wanted to arise (to leave). So when I saw him glancing at me, I mentioned to him the words of Ali ibn Bilal.

So he said to me: 'Did I not say to you that Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would perform Tawaaf by the House, and he would kiss the (Black) Stone, and the sanctity of the Prophet and the Believer is greater than sanctity of the House (Kaaba)? However, Allah Mighty and Majestic Commanded him that he should pause at Arafaat, and rather it is a place wherein Allah Loves that He be mentioned therein. Thus I loved it that you supplicate to Allah for me where Allah Loves that He be supplicated to'.

And he mentioned from him that he said, and did not memorise it from him, he said: 'But rather, these are places wherein Allah Loved that He be worshipped, thus I loved it that he should supplicate for me where Allah Loves that He be worshipped. Did you not say to him such and such?' He (the narrator) said, 'I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! If I was good similar to this, I would not have referred the matter upon you'. These are the words of Hashim, not my words'.
ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam prefer supplication in al-Hayr over the Kaaba?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia theological distinction between the sanctity of physical sites and the spiritual authority of the Imams, asserting that the Imam's presence warrants greater reverence than the Kaaba itself. Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that while ritual acts like kissing the Stone are valid, his preference for supplication in 'al-Hayr' reflects the divine will for worship to occur where God chooses, emphasizing the Imam's role as the locus of divine connection. This narrative underscores the concept of 'Hurma' (sanctity) extending beyond geography to the person of the Imam, a key tenet in Shia jurisprudence and theology.
